qa.name: Flexor Digitorum Profundus
qa.origin: Anterior and medial surfaces of the proximal three-quarters of the ulna and interosseous membrane
qa.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of the second through fifth digits
qa.innervation: Medial half — ulnar nerve; Lateral half — anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve
qa.function: Flexion of the distal interphalangeal joints, flexion of the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints, weak wrist flexion
qa.clinical_note: Only muscle that flexes the distal interphalangeal joint — has a dual nerve supply making it useful for distinguishing median versus ulnar nerve injuries

qa.name: Flexor Pollicis Longus
qa.origin: Anterior surface of the radius and adjacent interosseous membrane
qa.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
qa.innervation: Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve
qa.function: Flexion of the interphalangeal joint of the thumb, weak flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb
qa.clinical_note: Innervated exclusively by the anterior interosseous nerve — injury causes inability to flex the thumb tip; tested by the OK sign pinch test

qa.name: Pronator Quadratus
qa.origin: Anterior surface of the distal quarter of the ulna
qa.insertion: Anterior surface of the distal quarter of the radius
qa.innervation: Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve
qa.function: Pronation of the forearm — primary pronator of the forearm
qa.clinical_note: Primary pronator of the forearm regardless of elbow position — pronator teres assists only when speed or force is needed; lies deep to all other anterior forearm muscles
